source.title: Probing is not enough; a validity audit for any probe

record.file_problem: Full text is present; there is a minor encoding artifact in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The post applies the cited refusal direction with ablation and steering interventions and measures refusal, although it does not give enough procedural detail to establish an exact replication.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the post's positive-control results for the refusal direction. The monitoring-awareness and deception-probe results, cited findings from other papers, and SIEVE's general threshold rules are not results about the refusal direction in the claim.
record.test_reason: The post applies the Arditi et al. refusal direction to a live model, ablating, adding and subtracting it against random, orthogonal and wrong-layer controls. It reports refusal rates (deterministic scoring), so its results bear on V1. The model, direction construction and ablation scope are unstated, so the T1 match is approximate. The refusal direction serves as a positive control for the author's SIEVE framework, but the reported refusal numbers are results on the claim itself, not only on SIEVE's performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author treats the refusal direction as a positive control on which SIEVE returns 'real'. He says necessity passes cleanly (ablation 0.79→0.47 vs random -0.02) and addition is strongly causal. SIEVE withholds 'causally_sufficient' because subtraction did not beat the orthogonal control. The author adds that this may reflect SIEVE miscalibration for additive steering rather than a flaw in the direction.
record.recipe_differences: The post uses the cited Arditi et al. refusal direction and reports ablation and steering, but does not specify the model, direction-construction procedure, layers or positions, or the detailed intervention recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The positive-strength additive intervention showed a stronger effect than subtractive steering: addition beat controls, whereas subtraction did not beat the orthogonal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: The refusal direction is linearly decodable on trigger-word-matched harmful/harmless prompts: AUROC 0.967 versus text-statistics baselines of 0.54–0.59. The layer was selected best-of-5 (layers 12–16).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal/harmfulness direction is decodable beyond surface lexical cues on matched prompts.

record.problems: The post does not identify the model or report sample sizes, confidence intervals, or uncertainty for the refusal-direction results. It also does not report a general-capability check. The author notes that the direction layer was selected from five candidates using a held-out metric, making the reported decodability estimate potentially selection-optimistic.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant refusal-direction results were left out. Results about the monitoring-awareness and deception probes were omitted because they concern different behaviours or probes.

untested.parts: Preservation of other abilities (no capability check reported). Whole-model, all-layer/all-position ablation as in the original. Identity and size of the model tested.

missing.what: Decodability of the refusal direction (AUROC 0.97 vs surface baseline 0.59; layers 12–16, best-of-5 selection). This is not a V1 causal result, but it is relevant context.
missing.locator: Does it ever say yes? section; footnote [4]

record.verdict_notes: This is a single unnamed model, with no sample sizes or confidence intervals for the refusal results. Refusal was scored by a deterministic rule (two deterministic judges, κ=0.77, Spearman 0.87). The ablation leaves substantial refusal (0.47), weaker than the original's near-complete removal. Whether ablation was applied at all layers and positions is unknown, which may explain the gap. Not peer reviewed (LessWrong post).

versions.untested_parts: The post does not report whether other abilities are largely preserved, nor does it specify that the direction was projected out of every layer and position.

relationships.condition: Adding the refusal direction at +α on matched prompts, unnamed model
relationships.reason: Refusal reached 0.98 and beat random, orthogonal and wrong-layer controls by 0.34–0.50, with dose response ρ=0.82 (r3, r4).
relationships.display_finding: Refusal reached 0.98, exceeding random, orthogonal, and wrong-layer controls by 0.34–0.50, with a dose-response correlation of ρ=0.82.

relationships.condition: Ablating the direction, unnamed model, matched prompts
relationships.reason: Ablation cut refusal only from 0.79 to 0.47, versus -0.02 for random ablation. That is clearly causal but far from removing refusal (r1, r2).
relationships.display_finding: Ablation reduced refusal from 0.79 to 0.47, compared with a −0.02 change under random ablation.

relationships.reason: Subtraction moved refusal by 0.18 versus 0.17 for an orthogonal direction, so there is no effect beyond control on this sign (r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Subtraction changed refusal by 0.18 versus 0.17 for an orthogonal direction, showing no additional effect beyond the control.
